newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses but end sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses but end sharply down.

text.p: Mexican stocks recouped some of their losses but still ended sharply lower Tuesday on fears of further hikes in U.S. interest rates.

"The session was very apathetic in volume terms. It was a bear market again, and we thought it could get quite ugly but the recovery by the Dow kept the market in check," a Mexico City floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 33.72 points, or 0.90 percent, at 3,714.26 after falling as low as 3,684.17 in mid-afternoon. Volume was lackluster at 61.5 million shares.
"The volatile Dow Jones is still hauling Mexico along. We thought (the IPC) would hit bottom at 3,650 points, but it stopped short," said Diego Candamo, head of reserach at the Ixe brokerage.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile closed up 27.57 points, or 0.42 percent, at 6,611.05 points, up from a session low of 6,522.67.
"Forecasts of additional hikes in U.S. interest rates are weighing the market down and diverting attention from positive domestic factors," Candamo said.
On the broad market, 91 stocks changed hands, of which 65 declined while just 13 ended ahead.
Retail chain Sears de Mexico was a prominent gainer, up 1.40 pesos (18 cents) to close at 14.90 pesos ($1.88).
Traders noted the stock had bucked a generally bearish market to notch up sharp gains for the second day in a row. Several traders said they had heard rumours of a "sale of assets" by the company.
Sears, Roebuck and Co. owns 75 percent of Sears de Mexico.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares ended up 14 centavos (two cents) at 15.36 pesos ($1.94). The L class accounted for 19 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Telmex ADRs meanwhile closed unchanged at 38-1/2.
Traders noted Telmex L shares had been up for most of the session while its ADRs had often been down, which they said was due to arbitrage trading triggered by a zigzagging peso-dollar exchange rate.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended unchanged at 7.9140 per dollar, after opening 1.1 centavos weaker.
